q: Statement: A fire broke out in a cloth market because of faulty electric wiring in one shop. Courses of action: I. The electric wiring of the shops in the market should be inspected. II. All cloth markets in the country should be closed. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Inspecting the wiring deals with the stated cause of the fire. Closing every cloth market in the country is extreme and does not follow from one fire.

q: Statement: Patients at a rural health centre wait for hours because only one doctor visits, and only on three days a week. Courses of action: I. More doctors should be posted to the centre, or the doctor's working days increased. II. The centre should be closed because it is of little use. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: The problem is too little doctor time, so adding doctors or days solves it. Closing the centre would leave patients with no care at all.

q: Statement: Several schoolchildren in Faisalabad were bitten by stray dogs near their school. Courses of action: I. The city authorities should take steps to control stray dogs near the school. II. The bitten children should be given the anti-rabies vaccine as advised by doctors. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Action I prevents further bites, and action II protects the children already bitten. Each deals with a real part of the problem.

q: Statement: Wheat flour prices in a city rose sharply after some traders hoarded large stocks. Courses of action: I. People should stop eating bread. II. The government should check the traders' warehouses and act against hoarding. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Hoarding is the stated cause, so checking warehouses addresses it. Asking people to stop eating bread is impractical and does not fix the cause.

q: Statement: A survey shows that many students of a college do not know how to use the new online admission portal. Courses of action: I. The college should hold help sessions on using the portal. II. The college should stop online admissions altogether. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Help sessions fill the gap the survey found. Scrapping the portal throws away a useful system because some students need guidance.

q: Statement: Many dead fish were found in a lake near a town, and a factory upstream was recently seen draining waste into the stream that feeds the lake. Courses of action: I. The factory's waste should be tested, and the factory stopped from releasing untreated waste if it is the source. II. Fishing in the lake should be suspended until tests show the water is safe. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Action I checks and controls the likely source. Action II is a sensible temporary step to protect people until the water is proven safe. Both are practical.

q: Statement: Passengers at a city airport often miss their flights because of long queues at its single security counter. Courses of action: I. Security checks at the airport should be stopped. II. More security counters should be opened at busy times. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: The queue comes from having one counter, so opening more counters fixes it. Removing security checks would put passengers in danger.

q: Statement: A few cases of cholera were reported in one village after floods. Courses of action: I. Health teams should be sent to the village to treat patients and test the drinking water. II. The whole province should be declared a disaster zone. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Health teams address the cases and their likely source. A few cases in one village do not justify declaring a whole province a disaster zone.

q: Statement: A student fainted during morning assembly on a very hot day. Courses of action: I. Morning assemblies should be banned in all schools. II. The school should arrange shade and drinking water during assemblies on hot days. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Shade and water deal with the heat that caused the fainting. Banning assemblies everywhere because of one incident is extreme.

q: Statement: One student in a class developed a rash after using a new brand of soap. Courses of action: I. That brand of soap should be banned across the country. II. All students in the class should stop washing their hands. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: One rash in one person is not enough to ban a product nationwide, and stopping handwashing would harm health. Neither action follows.

q: Statement: Many buyers complain that a shop's weighing scale shows more weight than it actually gives. Courses of action: I. All the shops in the market should be closed. II. The weights and measures department should check the shop's scale. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Checking the scale deals with the complaint about one shop. Closing every shop in the market punishes people who did nothing wrong.

q: Statement: Floods damaged the only bridge of a town, cutting off villages on the far side from the town's hospital. Courses of action: I. The bridge should be repaired or a temporary crossing built as soon as possible. II. Emergency medical help, such as a mobile clinic or boat service, should be arranged for the cut-off villages meanwhile. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Action I restores the link, which takes time. Action II meets the urgent medical need until then. They work together, so both follow.

q: Statement: Bilal's car engine overheats whenever he drives in summer, and the mechanic found that the coolant level is very low. Courses of action: I. Bilal should have the coolant refilled and the system checked for leaks. II. Bilal should sell the car at once. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: The information points to the low coolant, so refilling it and checking for leaks is the sensible decision. Selling the car ignores a simple fix.

q: Statement: A hospital's records show that most patient falls in its wards happen at night after the lights are switched off. Courses of action: I. Dim night lights should be provided in the wards. II. Patients should not be allowed to get out of bed at all. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: The data link falls to darkness, so dim night lights address the cause. Keeping every patient in bed at all times is impractical and harmful.

q: Statement: A pharmacy finds that many bottles in a new batch of cough syrup have broken seals. Courses of action: I. The pharmacy should stop selling all its medicines. II. The pharmacy should not sell the bottles with broken seals and should report the batch to the supplier. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: The problem is limited to one batch, so holding back those bottles and reporting them is the right decision. Stopping all sales is far too extreme.

q: Statement: A college's pass rate in physics fell after its only physics teacher left in the middle of the year. Courses of action: I. The college should appoint a new physics teacher quickly. II. Extra classes should be arranged for students who missed lessons. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Appointing a teacher fixes the cause for the future, and extra classes repair the lessons already lost. Both follow from the information.

q: Statement: Ayesha has an important exam in two days but has developed a high fever. Courses of action: I. She should see a doctor. II. She should stay up all night studying despite the fever. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: A high fever needs medical attention, and recovering will help her sit the exam. Staying up all night while ill would make her worse.

q: Statement: A shopkeeper gave one customer the wrong change by mistake and corrected it when told. Courses of action: I. His shop licence should be cancelled. II. All shops in the area should be made to use only card payments. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: One honest mistake that was quickly corrected needs no action. Cancelling his licence is extreme, and forcing card payments on every shop does not follow.

q: Statement: Crops in a village often fail because canal water reaches it at irregular times, although groundwater is available. Courses of action: I. Farmers should be helped to use groundwater, such as through tube wells, in a careful way. II. The irrigation department should set a regular water schedule for the village. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Using the available groundwater gives farmers a backup, and a regular canal schedule fixes the main problem. Both use the information given.

q: Statement: A survey in a city finds that most dengue mosquito larvae are breeding in water collected in old tyres and uncovered water tanks. Courses of action: I. Citizens should be told to cover water tanks and empty or remove old tyres. II. Anti-mosquito spraying should be done only in the city's parks. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Action I targets exactly where the survey found the larvae. Action II ignores the data, since parks were not named as the main breeding sites.

q: Statement: A student got low marks in biology because he studied only from short notes and skipped the textbook. Courses of action: I. He should drop biology as a subject. II. He should study from the textbook along with his notes. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: The cause is skipping the textbook, so adding it to his study fixes the problem. Dropping the subject is an extreme reaction.

q: Statement: A school's results improved after it began holding short weekly tests. Courses of action: I. The school should stop all teaching and only hold tests. II. The school should continue the weekly tests. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: The information shows the weekly tests help, so continuing them is sensible. Tests cannot replace teaching, so action I does not follow.

q: Statement: Workers in a factory complain of hearing problems, and noise in the main hall is measured far above the safe limit. Courses of action: I. Workers should be given ear protection, and the noise reduced where possible. II. Workers' hearing should be tested at regular intervals. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Action I reduces the harm at its source, and action II detects damage early. Both are practical steps based on the measured problem.

q: Statement: Many students in a hostel get stomach infections because the water tank on its roof is never cleaned. Courses of action: I. The tank should be cleaned and covered regularly. II. Students should be advised to drink boiled or filtered water until then. III. The hostel should be shut down. Which course(s) of action follow?
o: I, II and III all follow
x: Cleaning the tank removes the cause, and safe drinking water protects students meanwhile. Shutting the hostel is extreme when the fault can be fixed.

q: Statement: A city hospital's emergency ward is overloaded because nearby districts have no emergency facilities. Courses of action: I. Emergency facilities should be set up in the district hospitals. II. The city hospital should refuse patients from other districts. III. The city hospital's emergency ward should be expanded meanwhile. Which course(s) of action follow?
o: I, II and III all follow
x: Action I removes the root cause and action III handles the load until then. Refusing emergency patients would put lives at risk, so II does not follow.

q: Statement: Shops in a market keep catching fire because of overloaded electric connections. Courses of action: I. The wiring should be inspected and overloaded connections fixed. II. Fire extinguishers should be placed in the market. III. Electricity to the market should be cut off permanently. Which course(s) of action follow?
o: I, II and III all follow
x: Fixing the wiring prevents fires and extinguishers limit damage if one starts. Cutting power for good would shut down the market, so III is extreme.

q: Statement: A survey finds that students who read books for pleasure write better essays. Courses of action: I. The college library should add more interesting books for general reading. II. Essay writing should be removed from the syllabus. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: The finding suggests that encouraging reading improves writing, so action I follows. Removing essays ignores the finding entirely.

q: Statement: A road accident occurred because a truck driver had been driving for 18 hours without rest. Courses of action: I. Rules limiting drivers' working hours should be enforced. II. All trucks should be banned from the roads. III. Transport companies should be checked to see that their drivers get proper rest. Which course(s) of action follow?
o: I, II and III all follow
x: Enforcing limits and checking companies both target driver tiredness. Banning all trucks would stop the transport of goods and is far too extreme.

q: Statement: Many children in a neighbourhood have not been vaccinated against measles. Courses of action: I. Health workers should run a vaccination drive in the area. II. Parents should be told why the vaccine is important. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: A vaccination drive reaches the children directly, and informing parents helps them accept it. Both actions address the problem.

q: Statement: A college's science laboratories stand unused because it has no laboratory assistants. Courses of action: I. The laboratories should be turned into storerooms. II. Laboratory assistants should be hired. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Hiring assistants solves the stated cause and lets students do practicals again. Turning labs into storerooms gives up on practical work.

q: Statement: Many vehicles speed on the busy road outside a primary school during school hours. Courses of action: I. Speed breakers and warning signs should be placed near the school. II. Traffic police should be posted at the school's opening and closing times. III. Children should be taught how to cross the road safely. Which course(s) of action follow?
o: I, II and III all follow
x: Speed breakers slow vehicles, police control traffic at the busiest times, and road-safety lessons protect the children. All three are practical.

q: Statement: A teacher found one student sleeping during a lecture. Courses of action: I. All lectures should be shortened to ten minutes. II. The student should be expelled from the college. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: One sleepy student does not justify changing every lecture, and expulsion is far too harsh for this. Neither action follows.

q: Statement: Many people do not file their income tax returns because the forms are hard to understand. Courses of action: I. The forms should be simplified. II. Help desks and online guides should be provided to assist people. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Simpler forms remove the difficulty, and help desks support those who still struggle. Both actions follow from the stated cause.

q: Statement: Doctors in a city link a rise in eye and skin infections to public swimming pools whose water is not properly treated. Courses of action: I. The pools' water should be tested and kept properly chlorinated. II. Swimming should be banned in the city forever. III. All public swimming pools in the city should be demolished. Which course(s) of action follow?
o: I, II and III all follow
x: Testing and treating the water removes the cause of the infections. A permanent ban on swimming and demolishing every pool are extreme steps that go far beyond fixing the problem.
